# mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member (Resource)

An instance in a load balancer pool: every address the instance has on the load balancer's network becomes a member, as one group. The console keeps the group in step with the instance: when it gains or loses nodes, they are added to or removed from the pool. The instance must be one of yours with an address on the load balancer's network. For a server outside the console, use `mtncloud_load_balancer_member`. One per instance and pool: the cloud adds and removes an instance's members together, so a second port for the same instance needs `mtncloud_load_balancer_member`. With `pin_address`, only that one address of the instance is added ("pin one node"): the console checks it is your instance's, then never adds to or removes it as the instance scales.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every address the instance has on the network joins the pool, and the pool follows the
# instance as it scales.
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member" "app" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  pool_id          = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id
  instance_id      = mtncloud_instance.app.id
  port             = 8080
}

output "app_members" {
  value = mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member.app.members[*].address
}

# Only one node of the instance, pinned: it stays when the instance scales, and no other node joins.
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member" "admin" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  pool_id          = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.admin.id
  instance_id      = mtncloud_instance.app.id
  pin_address      = mtncloud_instance.app.private_ip
  port             = 9090
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (Number) The instance, for example `mtncloud_instance.web.id`. A new instance can take up to a minute to be accepted. Changing it replaces the members.
- `load_balancer_id` (String) ID of the load balancer, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `network_id` (Number) ID of the MTN Network the load balancer is on, for example `mtncloud_network.app.id`. Your tenant must own it: a network shared with you is read-only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `pool_id` (String) The pool, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id`. Changing it replaces the members.
- `port` (Number) The port the instance listens on. Changing it replaces the members.

### Optional

- `backup` (Boolean) Only send traffic here when every other member is down. Defaults to `false`. Changing it replaces the members.
- `pin_address` (String) One of the instance's addresses on the load balancer's network, to add only that node. It stays a member when the instance scales, and other nodes aren't added. Leave it out for every node. Changing it replaces the member.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `weight` (Number) Each member's share of the traffic, 0 to 256; 0 sends them none. Defaults to `1`. Changing it replaces the members.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The instance's ID, as a string.
- `members` (Attributes List) The instance's members now, sorted by address. The list follows the instance as it scales. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.


<a id="nestedatt--members"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) The node's address.
- `id` (String) Member ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member.app <network_id>/<load_balancer_id>/<pool_id>/<instance_id>
# A pinned node: the instance's ID, then @ and the node's address.
terraform import mtncloud_load_balancer_instance_member.admin <network_id>/<load_balancer_id>/<pool_id>/<instance_id>@<address>
```
